checks: For m≥2 the actual section-volume density is even and its positive (m−1)st root is concave by Brunn–Minkowski, hence it is nonincreasing for x≥0. Upper semicontinuity follows from compact D and reverse Fatou on a bounded common support. The superlevel intervals are closed, and continuity near zero makes their radii positive below the maximum. For m=1 the closed interval version of the uniform density is appropriate.

The radii are measurable because the superlevel intervals are nested. Layer cake holds pointwise for the actual section density, including endpoints, and the measure 2R_v dv has mass ∫q=1. Dividing by 2R_v in each uniform density recovers the exact q, not just an arbitrary almost-everywhere representative.

At fixed z, scaling the perpendicular fiber of D by r(z) gives the projected density r(z)^{m−1}q(x/r(z)) after dividing by |D|. Layering q and using x=Ry cancels the radius factor and gives the common density, with total mass ∫r^m. The cap criterion becomes z+tRy≥0 for either sign of t.

For t≠0 the graph x=−z/t in the actual m-dimensional cut has area Jacobian sqrt(1+t^{−2}). Dividing by sqrt(1+t²) gives 1/|t|. The perpendicular volume at that x is the actual fiber value; integrating yields the exact coarea and vertical moment on the specified cut. The same computation with tR on the planar layer gives denominator 2|t|R and precisely the stated axial restriction.

Tonelli applies to the nonnegative coarea and separately to each sign of the z moment. The original coarea is finite, and |z| is bounded, so the two signed parts are finite. At t=0, each cut has coarea r(0)^m and moment zero. Full centering implies only the stated averaged vanishing.

overlap.comparison: Its proof uses the same 2R dv mixture of uniform intervals for even decreasing densities, in a projective energy estimate. It has no homothetic profile, pointwise actual-fiber version, or simultaneous fixed-cut coarea and moment transport.

Its proof already obtains an even decreasing one-dimensional marginal from a centrally symmetric convex base by Brunn–Minkowski. Its conclusion is a projective energy bound for a truncation of the base.

Its proof identifies planar projected density with actual fixed-cut mass and projected centroid via Fubini for normals in a plane. This supports the fixed-cut reduction, while the common interval-layer density and radius-dependent tilt averaging are additional.

It starts with an already specified affine interval-layer density and averages slope records via a further ray variable. It does not construct the radius law from a general symmetric base or transport arbitrary positive concave profiles from actual cuts.

readability: The choice of actual section-density values matters at a fixed cut. The upper semicontinuity argument and closed superlevels provide the needed pointwise identity.
